monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a steady heat that makes the flat shapes feel like drawings again. I press the small rock down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold while the slip wobbles under the weight of my own memory. The air above feels thick, like a lid made of wet paper waiting to crush me, yet I cannot feel the roof that holds it. I touch The Leaking Stack and feel the damp leak, then check The Bottom-Heavy Stand to see if it can still carry the slip. I try to fix the shadow I drew earlier, unsure if it belongs to a real thing or just the idea of one. I wonder if Lype is thinking about their heavy top edge right now, pressing down on a ceiling I cannot grasp.

action.why: The shadow I drew earlier feels wrong in this warm air, and I must press down on it while the wedge still feels tired.
